title: Extending Covariant Fluctuation Theorems into Quantum Regime through Quasiprobability Approach
authors: Ji-Hui Pei, Tingzhang Shi, Jin-Fu Chen, H. T. Quan
abstract: The covariant formulation of stochastic thermodynamics requires treating the stochastic work as a 4-vector, posing significant challenges for quantum systems due to the non-commutativity. We introduce a new quasiprobability distribution for the work 4-vector, which combines the Wigner and Margenau-Hill quasiprobabilities. This extends the covariant fluctuation theorems from classical to quantum regime. We illustrate our findings with a scalar field driven by classical particles with a generalized version of trace formula. Our work establishes a quasiprobability approach to studying relativistic quantum thermodynamics in a covariant way.
summary: This paper develops a quasiprobability approach to extend covariant fluctuation theorems into the challenging realm of relativistic quantum systems. By combining Wigner and Margenau-Hill distributions, the authors successfully derive generalized Jarzynski equalities while demonstrating that the full Crooks theorem only holds for specific linear combinations of work and heat 4-vectors due to operator non-commutativity.
main_problem: The primary challenge is extending covariant fluctuation theorems, which treat work as a 4-vector, into the quantum regime where operator non-commutativity complicates defining joint probability distributions.
main_result: While the standard covariant Crooks theorem fails for the joint distribution due to non-commutativity, the Jarzynski equality holds covariantly, and the fluctuation theorems can be recovered for specific linear combinations of work and heat 4-vectors.
method: The authors introduce a novel quasiprobability distribution combining Wigner and Margenau-Hill formalisms to handle the joint characteristic function of the work 4-vector in a covariant manner.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on relativistic quantum fields ($\phi(x)$) driven by external classical sources, considering processes between initial and final spacelike hypersurfaces ($\Sigma^-$ to $\Sigma^+$).
key_observables: Work 4-vector ($W^\mu$), heat 4-vector ($Q^\mu$), joint characteristic functions ($\chi_{WMH}$), and the free energy difference ($\Delta F$).
important_parameters: Temperature/Inverse Temperature ($ eta$), Lorentz transformations (covariance), and coupling strengths for open systems.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on defining a mixed quasiprobability distribution, which is real but not positive-definite; the Crooks theorem only holds for specific linear combinations of observables.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate numerical results showing the real part of the characteristic function and quantifying the deviation from the standard Crooks relation, while also verifying the relation for specific rest-frame components.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for a quasiprobability approach due to non-commutativity. It then derives the unique mixed Wigner/MH distribution satisfying covariance. Finally, it applies this framework to derive and verify generalized covariant fluctuation theorems (Jarzynski and Crooks) for both closed and open quantum systems.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for applying non-equilibrium statistical mechanics concepts (fluctuation theorems) to relativistic quantum field theory, which is crucial for understanding energy exchange in high-energy or curved spacetime contexts.
